summary: Team Alice built ATLAS OF MARS, an interactive web prototype for the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge. Using a Mars basemap based on NASA Viking imagery, users can mark a base or rover, draw a route, outline a hazard zone, and add notes. The same plan appears on a simulated spacesuit display. When the simulated connection is interrupted, the display keeps the last map it received. The project shows how a crew could prepare a surface excursion and carry its route, landmarks, and observations into the field on one shared map.
details:
ATLAS OF MARS connects a browser-based mission map with a simulated wrist display. Users can explore Mars by coordinates, place mission objects, and add routes, zones, pins, or notes. In our demo, the map shows a base, a rover, an astronaut marker, and a manually marked sandstorm zone. The wrist preview uses those same annotations, so the astronaut can see the plan prepared in the browser.

We built the prototype with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The demo runs in the browser, stores mission edits locally, and includes an offline map preview. The spacesuit concept places the display on the inner forearm. We considered screen readability and how the map should behave when a connection drops.

Our roadmap includes using the display to request a satellite relay or call a robotic rover. We also plan an AI assistant that monitors life-support readings, tracks the astronaut’s position, helps plan routes, and brings up relevant footage from rover and robot cameras when needed. These are proposed capabilities. The current prototype demonstrates map editing and a virtual display.
